newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine, IMF sign stand-by deal - c.bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine, IMF sign stand-by deal - c.bank chief.

text.p: The Ukrainian government and the International Monetary Fund signed a standby agreement worth about $700 million on Wednesday, Central Bank Chairman Viktor Yushchenko told a news conference.
"We are counting on receiving half of Ukraine's quota of $1.425 billion from the Fund by the end of the year. We are talking about $700-$800 million," Yushchenko said.
The loan was earlier expected to be anything between $550 million and $800 million.

Yushchenko said he and Prime Minister Valery Pustovoitenko had signed a memorandum negotiated with the IMF which is expected to be approved by the Fund's Board of Directors on August 25. "We can expect to receive the first tranche in September," Yushchenko said.

The stand-by deal is designed to see Ukraine through an interim period while it implements structural reforms to qualify for a delayed, three-year Extended Fund Facility previously estimated at $2.5-$3.0 billion.
The IMF's Kiev representative Goohoon Kwon has said the two sides would move quickly to negotations on an extended loan.
